Combined Risk & Opportunity Assessment

Residual view — after actions
ⓘ Gross view (before actions)
Risks: Negative Impact × Likelihood · Opportunities: Positive Impact × Feasibility.

Residual view (after actions)
Risks: Inherent Risk Level × Control effectiveness (weaker control toward the centre).
Opportunities: Opportunity Level × Realization (less realized toward the centre).

The "Arrow of Attention" (grey inverted triangle) narrows to the centre axis: the closer an item sits to the centre-top, the more attention it needs. Uses the map filters above (By BU view). The Excel export always includes both views.

Assessment cycles

Each BU re-assesses its risks and opportunities every 2–3 years. Every cycle is kept separately — starting a new one never overwrites an old one. Locked cycles are read-only. The Cycle selector at the top of the page decides what every tab, heat map and export shows.
The starting point's risks and opportunities are copied into the new cycle as a draft (scores = the consolidated scores of that cycle). Each copy keeps its ID and records it as its Previous-cycle ID, so BUs just update, add or close items.

BU review progress —

e.g. “R04-KSA (former 2023)” → “R04-KSA”, BU “KSA (former 2023)” → “KSA”. Preview first; clashes are left untouched.

Admin Settings

Manage every reference list used across the dashboard. Changes apply immediately everywhere — heat maps, dropdowns, and the risk register.

Scoring Scales

The 4 score levels (1\u20134) are fixed since all heat map math depends on them \u2014 only the label text is editable.

Group Family

Used to classify risks into the 7 SYSTRA group-level risk families.

Business Units (BU)

Used to tag which BU/region a risk or survey participant belongs to.

Status Options

Used in the risk register and edit panel's Status dropdown.

Custom Fields

Add, remove, or reorder extra columns that appear in the Risk Register table and each risk's edit panel. Supports text, date, and dropdown types. Changes apply immediately everywhere.

AI Settings Optional

Paste an OpenAI API key here to enable the "✨ Generate description" button in the risk edit panel. The key is stored only in your browser's localStorage — it never leaves your device. Do not use this if the file is hosted publicly or shared widely.

Admin PIN

Changes the PIN that unlocks Risk Universe, Sessions, and this Admin Settings tab. This is a soft deterrent, not strong security \u2014 anyone viewing the page source could find it.

Risk Universe — Default Titles & Descriptions

Review and edit the default title and description for each of the 36 Risk Universe categories. These auto-fill the edit panel when you add a new risk or click "Apply default". Changes are saved to this browser and synced to Firestore. You can also drop your full multi-tab ERM workbook here — it automatically picks the "Risk Universe Defaults" sheet.
Universe Category is now editable below, alongside Title and Description — edits and Excel uploads update the live Risk Universe list, not just the Title/Description text. Uploading updates matching codes and adds any new ones found in the file. Use "+ Add category" for a brand-new code, or 🗑 to remove one (codes themselves aren't renamed in place, to avoid breaking risks already tagged with them).
Code Universe Category Default Title Default Description

Group Family ↔ Risk Universe Mapping

Define which Risk Universe categories belong to each Group Family. This drives the hierarchical view on the Risk Landscape tab — clicking a Group Family bubble shows its universe subcategories. Fully editable: drag codes between families or use the dropdowns. Changes save to Firebase encrypted like all other admin data. You can also drop your full multi-tab ERM workbook here — it automatically picks the "Mapping to Group Risk" sheet.

Import Risk Data

Bulk add or update risks from an Excel or CSV file. Matching Risk IDs are updated; new IDs are added to the register.
Expected column format (click to expand)
Risk IDOptional — leave blank to auto-assign the next available ID.
TitleRequired — short risk name.
DescriptionOptional — full risk description (also accepts "Final Description").
Group FamilyOptional — should match an existing Group Family, managed above.
Risk UniverseOptional — use the "CODE_Label" format, e.g. C7_Cybersecurity attacks and system compromise.
BUOptional — Business Unit code, e.g. FRA, IND, USA, managed above.
OwnerOptional — risk owner's name.
StatusOptional — defaults to "Ongoing" if blank, managed above.
Likelihood / Impact / ControlOptional, default to 2 — accepts a number 1–4 or label text (e.g. "Rare", "High", "Defined").
CycleOptional — the cycle name (e.g. 2026). Blank = the cycle chosen above the drop zone.
Previous-cycle IDOptional — this risk's ID in the previous cycle, to track it across cycles.
Column headers are flexible and can appear in any order. Tip: the Risk Register's CSV export uses these exact column names — edit it in Excel and re-import to round-trip safely. You can also drop your full multi-tab ERM workbook here — it automatically finds the "Risk Register" sheet.
Optional columns: Cycle (a cycle name — overrides the choice above for that row) and Previous-cycle ID (links the record to last cycle's ID). Locked cycles are never changed.

Import Opportunity Data

Bulk add or update opportunities from an Excel or CSV file. Matching Opportunity IDs are updated; new IDs are added to the Opportunity Register. Stored encrypted in Firestore (erm_opportunities).
Expected column format (click to expand)
IDOptional — leave blank to auto-assign the next O-number (e.g. O04-FRA).
TitleRequired — short opportunity name.
DescriptionOptional — full description.
Group Family / Risk UniverseOptional — same values as the Risk Register (Risk Universe in "CODE_Label" format).
BUOptional — Business Unit code, e.g. FRA, IND, GLT.
Owner / StatusOptional — status defaults to "Ongoing".
Positive Impact1–4 or label: Low · Medium · High & Significant · Discerning & Strategic.
Feasibility1–4 or label: Very limited · Difficult · Possible · Ready to be achieved.
RealizationOptional, defaults to 1 — 1–4 or label: Not started · Initiated · In progress · Realized. Used for the residual combined map.
Linked Risk ID (Duality)Optional — a Risk ID from the Risk Register (e.g. R11) to create a Duality pair.
CycleOptional — the cycle name (e.g. 2026). Blank = the cycle chosen above the drop zone.
Previous-cycle IDOptional — this opportunity's ID in the previous cycle.
Headers are flexible and can be in any order. The template's second sheet lists valid BUs, Group Families, Risk Universe codes and current Risk IDs. A multi-tab workbook works too — the sheet whose name contains "Opportunit" is picked automatically.
Optional columns: Cycle (a cycle name — overrides the choice above for that row) and Previous-cycle ID (links the record to last cycle's ID). Locked cycles are never changed.

Opportunity scales: Positive Impact — Low (1) / Medium (2) / High & Significant (3) / Discerning & Strategic (4). Feasibility — Very limited (1) / Difficult (2) / Possible (3) / Ready to be achieved (4). Level = Positive Impact × Feasibility (1–16). Realization — Not started (1) / Initiated (2) / In progress (3) / Realized (4).
Duality — a risk that is simultaneously an opportunity. The risk stays in the Risk Register; the opportunity is added here and linked via the Linked Risk ID.
